abstract_sentences.text: Contrastive learning has become a cornerstone of modern representation learning, allowing training with massive unlabeled data for both task-specific and general (foundation) models.
A prototypical loss in contrastive training is InfoNCE and its variants.
In this work, we show that the InfoNCE objective induces Gaussian structure in representations that emerge from contrastive training.
We establish this result in two complementary regimes.
First, we show that under certain alignment and concentration assumptions, projections of the high-dimensional representation asymptotically approach a multivariate Gaussian distribution.

evidence.anchor: under certain alignment and concentration assumptions

abstract_sentences.text: Next, under less strict assumptions, we show that adding a small asymptotically vanishing regularization term that promotes low feature norm and high feature entropy leads to similar asymptotic results.
We support our analysis with experiments on synthetic and CIFAR-10 datasets across multiple encoder architectures and sizes, demonstrating consistent Gaussian behavior.

evidence.anchor: synthetic and CIFAR-10 datasets across multiple encoder architectures

abstract_sentences.text: This perspective provides a principled explanation for commonly observed Gaussianity in contrastive representations.

evidence.anchor: principled explanation for commonly observed Gaussianity

abstract_sentences.text: The resulting Gaussian model enables principled analytical treatment of learned representations and is expected to support a wide range of applications in contrastive learning.

evidence.anchor: wide range of applications in contrastive learning

final_judgment.single_storyline: Population InfoNCE decomposes into alignment and uniformity; HGR bounds alignment, plateau or vanishing regularization selects spherical uniformity, and thin-shell/radial control plus spherical CLT yields fixed-dimensional Gaussian projections.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps Eq.4, Eq.6, route assumptions, core corollary/proposition/theorem conclusions, CV/AD/DP diagnostics, matched supervised control, main tables and explicit asymptotic/optimization caveats.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A–C move proofs and projection rates; D moves generalized plateau/vMF stationary analysis; E moves implementation, dataset/augmentation/optimization details and Figures 6–11.
final_judgment.best_pattern: A two-route theory is paired with a mechanism-aligned experiment sequence: Fig.2 alignment/uniformity, Fig.4 dynamics, and Table 1 supervised control.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Coordinate-wise AD/DP and norm CV do not establish joint multivariate Gaussianity; plateau feasibility, Align(σ)=η² and optimizer attainment also lack direct empirical verification, while pretrained/application claims are bounded extensions.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: Pair every asymptotic condition with a same-concept finite-sample diagnostic and add a control that can alter the mechanism explanation; state population optimality separately from training attainability.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The rule applies to representation objectives with explicit population laws and identifiable high-dimensional limits; downstream decisions, joint distributions, optimization dynamics or deployment require their own evidence.
final_judgment.theory_count: 10 unique theorem-like statements, 6 explicit proof blocks, and 28 raw theorem-label matches including references.
